reading.en: C, unasserted, is stronger at the first step: a costless addition is better, not merely not worse, even of a life not worth living, as admission reads no quality. It leaves mixed comparisons unranked, so neither yields nor blocks the later steps. 08 lists the results as unstated. The condition fixes scope, C order. [AI reading]

says.en: Stated by prior frameworks and not yet here: 'Parfit's mere addition, the Repugnant Conclusion and the non-identity problem (C ranks a costless addition better; the philosophy dossier keeps what it owes open)'.
[this dossier, AI]: C 'also ranks adding a life not worth living as better, against the procreation asymmetry'; 'it neither yields nor blocks the paradox's later steps'.
AI reading: the generations a poisoning forecloses 'occur nowhere on the course taken, so they lie on no line'; a loss is read by comparing courses.

account_adds.en: Admission as what is compared, which sets this comparison up differently from welfare totals.

source_adds.en: The puzzles themselves, as tests C has not faced; 07 does not show the value of new lives.

name.en: Parfit: theories directly collectively self-defeating

source.work: D. Parfit, Reasons and Persons (1984)
source.locator: Part I ch. 4

sense.en: In each-we dilemmas, if each successfully follows an agent-relative theory, the aims it gives each are worse achieved than if none had. Common-sense morality is so self-defeating in many-person cases, and should be revised there.

reading.en: Two forms. The accounting law has the many-person case for one condition: each within what a step gives, together past it. Nearer his own is `Weighting.Restraint`, a prisoner's dilemma read as a menu: widening a shared menu lowers what each gets at the one mutual best response, while every order meeting C ranks the wider above. 07 calls that a conflict, no inconsistency, and asks whether any course has the shape. C and the condition stay unasserted. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World: balance; for the ending, activity needing support, only active giving, the gate local): 'Formations can each take within what a step gives while together they take more' (`Pair.own_not_joint`). Verdict in 08: near-definitional.

Witness on a listing's frame: 'widening the one menu both choose from can lower what each gets by the game's payoffs'; 'That is no inconsistency'; 'neither reading is shown to be the one that counts'. Open: if a course of what can form has this shape, 'the menu witness stands against C there'.

account_adds.en: The point of no return for a gated condition, whatever each drawer's own draw; on the menu, that where no choice bears on another's a widening cannot lower what each gets.

source_adds.en: His criterion: a theory so self-defeating is to be revised there. 07 stops short: 'neither reading is shown to be the one that counts'.

name.en: Parfit: mistakes in moral mathematics

source.work: D. Parfit, Reasons and Persons (1984)
source.locator: Part I ch. 3

sense.en: An act can be wrong though it makes no difference or none perceptible, since it may be one of a set of acts that together harm. To judge by one's own share, or to ignore small or overdetermined effects, is a mistake.

reading.en: The record names the comparison, 'from the AI's prior knowledge, not newly read'. The law gives the form: parts that make a difference only together, while no member alone does, and the overdetermined case is 'my share makes no difference'. It stops before his conclusion: neither test 'yields responsibility or duty', and no law calls the act wrong. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any process; withholding a supplied map; the move taken held fixed): parts make the difference together while no member alone does exactly where they make it together and withholding any one leaves the same move breaking it (`Dependence.differenceOnlyTogether_iff`). In the witness Pool the first drawer's part makes no difference.

account_adds.en: The exact condition, and that but-for and participation come apart; only for the single-part, run-level test, the record says.

source_adds.en: The moral claim itself, that each act in such a set is wrong; and imperceptible harms (the harmless torturers).

name.en: Parfit: the present-aim theory and the attack from two sides

source.work: D. Parfit, Reasons and Persons (1984)
source.locator: Part II, chs. 6 to 8

sense.en: Self-interest is temporally neutral yet agent-relative, and so is unstable: it can be attacked from the present-aim side, by those who deny the first, and from the moral side, by those who deny the second. Neither neutrality is forced, and treating them apart is arbitrary.

reading.en: The present-aim evaluator stands in a record as who escapes the route from own good, and a significance bounded in time as a rival: that is where his attack from the present-aim side lands. The other side does not map: the step's two forms split by drawing and by standpoint, and a drawing varies a region, not a time. His instability argument is not stated, and the link is this reader's. The condition for scope and C for order stay unasserted. [AI reading]

says.en: Not shown: 'a present-aim evaluator meets the other premises and gives the formed other no significance'.
Theorem (any type; World witness): a significance caring only for continuations up to a step is a rival of the condition wherever there is a standpoint and a formation.

account_adds.en: Witnesses of each rival; P-15's question on cutoffs against discounting.

source_adds.en: The argument from instability, which would bear directly on P-11's de se case.

name.en: Parfit: normative truths and convergence

source.work: D. Parfit, On What Matters (2011)
source.locator: vol. 1 ch. 16 (Triple Theory); vol. 2 Part Six (non-naturalism); locators from memory

sense.en: There are irreducibly normative truths, not natural facts, and reasons are not given by desires. The best Kantian, contractualist and consequentialist theories converge, climbing one mountain from different sides, and such convergence supports that there are such truths.

reading.en: T5 has a convergence claim, and a much narrower one: a bound on where those counting everything positively can disagree. It reduces to a shared partial order, with C's premise relocated, and is proved only for net weightings; mixed cases stay open. No normative fact underlies it; warrant stays open for both premises, the condition for scope and C for order. [AI reading]

says.en: T5: the reduction proved for net weightings, the bound conjectured; 'That valuers value positively is C's premise relocated'; VD1 failed, VD2 passed in part, role-play, human valuers untested.
Not shown: 'That the continuation condition, C or the step of invariance is warranted. No warrant binding every possible mind is claimed'.

account_adds.en: A theorem under the convergence, and frozen tests that failed in part.

source_adds.en: A realist account of what warrant would be; the account has no metaethical position (P-02's question).

name.en: Ontic structural realism: there are no things, or none prior to structure

source.work: J. Ladyman and D. Ross, Every Thing Must Go (2007); S. French, The Structure of the World (2014); M. Esfeld and V. Lam (2008) for the moderate form
source.locator: Ladyman and Ross chs. 1 to 3

sense.en: Physics, especially permutation invariance in quantum theory, supports that the world's structure is what exists: relata either are not self-subsistent or exist only as nodes (eliminative or moderate forms). Structure is modal and objective.

reading.en: 08 names it as a neighbour with no argument. The representation has this shape: configurations, laws and parts 'need no determination beyond relations', and labels carry nothing. Scope: shown of what is represented, argued of the theory, 'Neither shows that reality has none'. The thesis's sentence is as ontic as OSR's, yet its stated content is a demand on explanation and its warrant is not physics. Its model keeps relata told apart by equality on the carrier. [AI reading]

says.en: 'These show that configurations, laws and parts, as represented, need no determination beyond relations; that the theory as a whole needs no independent entity is argued, not proved. Neither shows that reality has none.' 'Its neighbours are ontic structural realism (Ladyman and Ross 2007) ...'
Theorem (World): 'Labels carry nothing': a renaming preserves the five readings checked, 'while the pattern of names across steps carries identity'.
Calibration (World): 'Identity read off relations is identity up to indiscernibility'; 'names carry one decided identity more than relations do'.

account_adds.en: Three cases that look like refuters, and the laws that settle them; the nearest case against, equality on the carrier.

source_adds.en: The arguments from physics, the modal claim, and the debate between eliminative and moderate forms. 'Relations need relata' is named in 08 as live and not worked through.

name.en: Ladyman and Ross: the principle of naturalistic closure

source.work: J. Ladyman and D. Ross, Every Thing Must Go (2007)
source.locator: ch. 1

sense.en: Metaphysics is to be taken seriously only if it unifies hypotheses that current science motivates, and fundamental physics constrains the rest. A metaphysics argued from intuition or from a domestic picture of things is to be discontinued.

reading.en: By this rule the account's thesis has a problem it admits: 'By this section's measure the thesis has no strength'. It is argued from representations, and classical texts are among its readings. Its explanatory reading does meet his form: it takes explanation as deriving many conclusions from few patterns, counts them, and reports a tie with a rival dropping the word. A neighbour who might accept that test and not the neighbourhood. [AI reading]

says.en: 'By this section's measure the thesis has no strength: it excludes no observation, and the argument is that none could refute it. That is argued, not proved.'

'Proofs check relations under a representation, empirical work tests realization and correspondence, and philosophy examines constitutive identities. No cultural origin validates or disqualifies a method.'

'A theory explains, on the account taken here, by deriving many conclusions from few patterns of argument'; 'On a first count, at the grain of §7's shared laws, there is a tie'; 'A tie does not make the reading false.'

account_adds.en: An open statement of its thesis's strength, and a separate standing for each kind of claim.

source_adds.en: A rule for what metaphysics may be, which would put the thesis outside; the account does not answer it by name.

name.en: Dennett, Ross and Ladyman: to be is to be a real pattern

source.work: D. Dennett, 'Real Patterns' (1991); J. Ladyman and D. Ross, Every Thing Must Go (2007)
source.locator: Ladyman and Ross ch. 4, rainforest realism

sense.en: A pattern is real if it supports projection and compresses information relative to a physically possible computer, at its scale. What exists is relative to scale and is not reducible to one level; there are many real grains with no privileged one.

reading.en: A class closed under the relation adds nothing when read through: lumpability, here constancy, and grain-relative, as the account's classes are. A class named for a domain can fail by a smaller class explaining more, near to a compression test. No live page names the view; 'real' is not said of any class. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (root): for a class `E`, constancy is exactly that `R` read through the class adds nothing, `E;R;E ⊆ R;E` (`«闭合当且仅当有常»`). The record calls the law the relational analogue of lumpability, 'a correspondence not proved here'.

A class named for a domain can be defeated by 'two members alike under the class going on differently beyond measured error, another class of no more variables leaving less of the next state unaccounted for'. As a language, nothing could.

account_adds.en: A core for each class, and a named test (T2 has this form, AI reading).

source_adds.en: An existence criterion and an information measure. The account's reading does not say which classes are real; 'a class is warranted' is not shown.

name.en: Leibniz: the identity of indiscernibles

source.work: G. W. Leibniz, Discourse on Metaphysics (1686) §9; Correspondence with Clarke; M. Black, 'The Identity of Indiscernibles' (1952), for the two spheres
source.locator: as named

sense.en: No two things are exactly alike in every respect. Two things are never merely numerically different; a purely extrinsic difference would make no sense. Black's two spheres in an otherwise empty space is the standard counterexample.

reading.en: Asked as a universal, 08's calibrations give where it holds: identity read off relations is identity up to indiscernibility, and that this is decided is excluded middle over every world. Twin successors are Black's spheres in the model, and equality on the carrier separates them. 08's neighbour is the relational form: Leibniz asks a difference in intrinsic denomination, what the thesis refuses to explain by. Whether reality has such twins the account does not say. [AI reading]

says.en: Calibration (World): 'Identity read off relations is identity up to indiscernibility'; asked of every world, that indiscernibility is decided is exactly excluded middle; 'names carry one decided identity more than relations do'.
Theorem (any process): 'Naming the configurations makes sense exactly where alike configurations are one, which fails for twin successors of one move (`identifiesAlike_id_iff`).'
'The thesis would be empty if "relation" meant whatever difference turns up, as the identity of indiscernibles is trivial if any property counts.'

account_adds.en: The calibration of what deciding identity costs.

source_adds.en: The principle as true of what exists, its ground in sufficient reason, and difference as finally intrinsic.

name.en: Sen: the intersection approach

source.work: A. Sen, Collective Choice and Social Welfare (1970); 'Interpersonal aggregation and partial comparability' (1970); 'On Weights and Measures' (1977)
source.locator: Collective Choice chs. 7 and 7*

sense.en: Where weights are not fully known or agreed, take the judgments every admissible weighting shares. They form a quasi-ordering, incomplete and still usable, with partial comparability as a range between no comparison and full.

reading.en: Credited at the home: widening is what every positive weighting shares, the finite two-valued case. The weighted-ratio law states part of the graded case. C, calling the shared part better, is the account's premise, not Sen's, and unasserted, as is the condition that fixes scope. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type; finite listing, two-valued admission). 'This is Sen's intersection approach, and Pareto dominance as the unanimity of positive weightings'; 'Monotonicity at the standpoint is C's premise relocated: weaker, still a premise.'

Every positive weighting whose weights stand within n/d of each other ranks the course keeping p items above the one keeping q exactly where n q < d p. 08 lists this as Sen's graded comparisons already stated.

account_adds.en: Any class of orders from positive weightings up to every order ranking each widening higher (`Weighting.widens_iff_every_of_class`).

source_adds.en: Any admissible set of weights over real-valued welfare, and partial comparability as a family of ranges between none and full. The weighted-ratio law is one such range, on kept counts.

name.en: Sen: capability as the space of evaluation

source.work: A. Sen, 'Equality of What?' (1980); Commodities and Capabilities (1985); 'Welfare, Preference and Freedom' (1991); Development as Freedom (1999)
source.locator: as named; locators from memory

sense.en: Assess a person's position neither by utility nor resources but by capability: the set of beings and doings she has real freedom to achieve, which she has reason to value. Selecting and weighing functionings is left to public reasoning, and rankings may be partial. Against counting options, the worth of a freedom is not independent of what one prefers or has reason to value.

reading.en: 'What can form' has the shape of a capability set, and 07's chooser route brings it nearer: a course widens another exactly when no chooser does worse from it and some does better, Foster's effective freedom with every preference admitted. There Sen parts: that range counts 'a merely possible chooser', and he reads freedom by what a person has reason to value. His bearer is a person; C, unasserted, counts any admitted formation, with scope from the condition. [AI reading]

says.en: 'One course widens another exactly when no chooser does worse from it by its own valuation and some does better by its own'; 'what is assumed instead is that a merely possible chooser counts'; 'the chooser route is Foster's effective freedom with every preference admitted'. 'This does not derive C from anything and gives no reason for it.'
How two courses differ in what can form: closest prior 'opportunity sets (Pattanaik and Xu 1990)', near-definitional; the rankings by diversity not stated.
'The lexical order is the two-tier order read on realized claims, then reachable ranges, near Sen's achievement and freedom (1985).'; near-definitional or a witness.
Not shown: 'The value of bringing new lives into existence, well-being beyond admitted continuation, and constraints on acts.'
Reading [AI, D45]: 'Capability is reach, and the gap is the reach closure less the coupling closure'; another sense of the word.

account_adds.en: Widening over courses and steps, not one person's present set; what a course keeps reachable; what a range of choosers needs, and three witnesses where the route stops.

source_adds.en: Functionings valued by reasons, and well-being as what they are for. 07's RP alone mentions 'resources or capabilities', in passing. A process study (GAP-MAP §6.2) says the capability approach is never weighed against C.

name.en: Sen: the process aspect of freedom

source.work: A. Sen, Rationality and Freedom (2002); Development as Freedom (1999)
source.locator: Rationality and Freedom, introductory ch. and chs. 20 to 21; locators from memory

sense.en: Freedom has an opportunity aspect, what one can achieve, and a process aspect, how it comes about. Being forced to do what one would have chosen differs from choosing it, even at the same outcome; opportunity alone misses this.

reading.en: Widening reads only what is admitted, and 07 now says so: 'Nothing in a course's admitting a formation makes the formation chosen', and where admission is imposed a widening can stand below what it widens on a net weighting. Under the priority of basic conditions alternatives realizing the same claims compare alike unless the acting part is adjoined. That is his objection in the account's own terms. Condition for scope, C for order, both unasserted. [AI reading]

says.en: 'Where admission is imposed, an item a net weighting counts below zero can put a widening below what it widens'; 'Nothing in a course's admitting a formation makes the formation chosen, so whether what a course adds is left by a chooser or imposed is not shown'.

Conditional (J1/J2): 'alternatives realizing the same claims are compared alike'; adjoined as a basic claim, the acting formation's part orders them. 'Neither which is worse nor that the acting part is basic is shown.'
Reading [AI, D65; a historical correspondence, no theorem]: 'a reform is judged by who decides admission, comparison and correction next round'.

account_adds.en: The exact point at which the comparison goes blind, what would adjoin it, refusal as an item in every menu, and a witness of imposed admission.

source_adds.en: Process as a value in itself; agency as distinct from well-being. J4's 'legitimate feasible choice' and the direction's 'effective opportunities to understand, challenge and revise' are a premise and a proposal, not this.

name.en: Sen: adapted preferences misreport deprivation

source.work: A. Sen, Commodities and Capabilities (1985); On Ethics and Economics (1987)
source.locator: locator unverified; the hopeless beggar and tamed housewife passages

sense.en: People long deprived come to want little and take pleasure in small mercies, so a metric of desire or happiness reads their condition as fine. Their reports are formed by what they suffer and cannot serve alone as the measure of it.

reading.en: A reading formed from what the selection has done reads the share, not what lies beyond it; a loss so unread leaves the loop as it was. 07's chooser witness has the split he needs, a chooser gaining by its own order while what it takes stands lower in the order reading the result (07 credits Strotz; the Sen reading is mine). That readers are minds is a reading: 'none says a loss is a harm'. The condition, C and D stay unasserted. [AI reading]

says.en: Reading [AI, D65]: 'Later endorsement cannot authorize the formation that produced it.'

Theorem (any type): where neither the next share nor the rule read reads the beyond (`Unread`), courses alike in share and rule stay alike; 'a change of the reading of any size is absorbed' where the reading too is formed monotonically from the share. Not shown: that any actual rule is so formed.
Premise D, not asserted: 'every position with access to a response securing new living content has a contributory reason for it, whatever its endorsement'.

'Where the chooser's order is not the order reading the result, the chooser can gain and what it takes stand lower in that order' (`Weighting.AnotherReads`), which 07 says 'has the shape of Strotz's inconsistency'.

account_adds.en: The exact premise under which the reading moves nothing.

source_adds.en: What to read instead: capability. The account's answer is a reading of what lies beyond the share, by whoever reads it.

name.en: Sen: choice does not reveal welfare; commitment

source.work: A. Sen, 'Behaviour and the Concept of Preference' (1973); 'Rational Fools' (1977)
source.locator: as named

sense.en: Consistency of choice yields a binary relation and no measure of welfare. Commitment, acting against one's own expected welfare, drives a wedge between choice and welfare; a person reduced to a preference ordering is a rational fool.

reading.en: The law on choices stops where Sen does: what acts show is a shown relation and its reach, and nothing whose good it is. 07's chooser witness has the wedge in form: a chooser can gain by its own order while what it takes stands lower in the order reading the result. It says nothing of why the orders part, so the account has no commitment as a kind. 08's 'Sen (1977)' is not clearly this paper. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (root; no premise; near-definitional): the choices show `x` above `y` where `x` was chosen while `y` was open; the positive comparisons every such order shares are exactly the shown reach.
AI reading: 'Motivation is apart: that a loss counts from one's standpoint moves no one by itself.'
'Where the chooser's order is not the order reading the result, the chooser can gain and what it takes stand lower in that order' (`Weighting.AnotherReads`).

account_adds.en: Revealed preference on the root, with what no choice data separates. It bears on the ethics only under the two premises, the condition for scope and C for order, neither asserted.

source_adds.en: Commitment as a distinct ground of action, and the several concepts 'preference' confounds.

name.en: Sen: maximal choice, comparative justice

source.work: A. Sen, 'Maximization and the Act of Choice' (1997); The Idea of Justice (2009)
source.locator: Idea of Justice, Introduction and ch. 4

sense.en: Reasoned choice does not need a complete ranking: pick an option not worse than any other. Justice needs comparison of feasible alternatives and no account of the perfect arrangement. Incompleteness may be assertive, and is not a defect.

reading.en: C has the first half: it decides no mixed comparison. The maximal route is stated: with the comparison weakly decided on the menu an undefeated option exists, and L leaves a response with one good and one bad outcome incomparable both ways. No live line joins these to Sen; that join is this reader's. They are laws of choice, not ethics: the choosing rests on J1/J2 beside the condition for scope and C for order, none asserted. [AI reading]

says.en: 'On a reading of `living`, C ranks a course above each course it extends there ... and decides no other pair'; 'Choices take more, following from neither the condition nor C'.

Calibration: 'That every nonempty listed set of options at a frame's step, under an irreflexive transitive comparison, has an undefeated option is exactly weak excluded middle'; 'with the comparison weakly decided on the menu the option exists (`Requirement.frontier_exists`)'. L: 'a response with one good and one bad outcome is incomparable both ways.'

targets.part: the Calibration and Lifting and choice just below this anchor; the calibration has no record of its own

says.en: Premises as named at P-21: J1–J4: 'complete comparison with retained losses, priority of basic conditions, bounded responsibility, legitimate feasible choice', each a hypothesis where used. Whether J1's 'complete comparison' (08's card: 'retained losses') asks a complete order, the gloss does not settle.

account_adds.en: A calibration: that every nonempty listed menu has an undefeated option is exactly weak excluded middle.

source_adds.en: Comparative justice against an account of the perfect arrangement, and assertive incompleteness: a judgment that two are not comparable, not a gap in information.

name.en: Sen: the impossibility of a Paretian liberal

source.work: A. Sen, 'The Impossibility of a Paretian Liberal' (1970)
source.locator: article as a whole

sense.en: Unrestricted domain, weak Pareto and a minimal liberty for each person over a personal sphere cannot all hold in a social choice with no cycle. Unanimity can conflict with even minimal rights.

reading.en: The account's unanimity is on admission, not preferences, so the theorem does not transfer directly. Nearest is 07 §4.4's standpoints route, a Pareto relation among self-concerned orders: 'an order ranking below every widening that adds nothing to its own', read there as positional concern, stops the relation, the shape of a meddling preference: a proposal here, no stated form. No personal sphere is stated, nor whether one can conflict with widening. Condition for scope, C for order, unasserted. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: A proved limit on unanimity plus liberty. A study names it (foundation-assessment/GOVERNANCE-LITERATURE.md), and ig-integration-gaps/GAP-MAP.md §6.1 flags it, with Arrow, as unstated. P-04's question on rights and constraints is where it would go.

read: 07 what the chapter does not show

name.en: Sen: positional objectivity

source.work: A. Sen, 'Positional Objectivity', Philosophy & Public Affairs 22 (1993)
source.locator: article as a whole

sense.en: What one observes depends on one's position, yet observation from a position is interpersonally checkable by anyone who takes it. Objectivity need not be a view from nowhere; a positional view can still be mistaken as a trans-positional claim.

reading.en: Only the first half agrees: no view from nowhere, knowers inside the unfolding, de se apart from de dicto. His test is invariance at one position: same position, same observation, whoever takes it. 03's objectivity runs across differences of access, and counts checks 'only where they are differently vulnerable'; two at one position share a vulnerability, which is why his positional illusion survives the check. So his check is one the account would not count alone. Assessment standing, no law. [AI reading]

says.en: Assessment, continuity and objectivity: 'Objectivity is answerability to the relations a judgment concerns across differences of access, not consensus; shared inquiry adds checks only where they are differently vulnerable'.
'Knowing, modelling and criticizing happen inside it too, so their adequacy is part of the inquiry, not a vantage outside it.'

Theorem (any type): where each witness added copies one on the roster, inspection gives the same certificate; 'That a witness merely agreeing with another, without copying it, adds nothing is not shown.'

account_adds.en: The law of copied witnesses, on copies only; that checks count only where differently vulnerable is 03's assessment, not a law.

source_adds.en: Objectivity at one position as a kind of its own, positional illusion as a named error, and the transposition test.

changes.why: second critic (label): Memory against memory, the sense matches Adventures of Ideas ch. VII, the two 08 homes are copied faithfully, and fresh-reading and agreement of thesis-or-method hold. But 'agrees against imposition only' misses 01's reading D65, where three World premises hold 'by what their terms are', the form of his immanence on one model, and 08 §12's limit that calling an input immanent does not discharge it; both are added and the reading and source_adds amended.

second critic (label): Memory against memory, the sense matches Science and the Modern World ch. III and V. 08 §1 itself states the part, every split drawn 'together with what they leave out' and a separate type asserting no fundamental separation, with 08's head putting the real assumptions in the modelling: content the account states, not a law read onto him, so carried-in-part, source_adds as it is.

The first half's agreement with «分叉» as law stands, so carried-in-part with 07#step as a second carrier.

live_flags.what: 'deriving many conclusions from few patterns of argument' has the form of Kitcher's unification account, and 08 §9's 'judged by what it forbids' of Popper; neither name occurs on the live account (grep of chapters, fronts, review, records). A possibly missing credit.
